html:
SMTO-EXE-0149 — SMTO blocked a password field's contents from being read

GUID: 0383efe1-b384-57f3-a97f-f366528b06b3
Slug: ui-secure-value-read-forbidden
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • The Gateway tried to send back what's inside a password or other protected field, and SMTO refused it to keep that secret private. The secret wasn't shown or saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On the computer running the Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses on that computer), type the password or secret yourself directly into the app. SMTO never reads or types passwords, so this step always has to be done by you.
  2. Reply in the SMTO conversation to say you've finished, without including the password itself. SMTO can then carry on with the rest of the task.
  3. Select Copy error details and send them, with the app name, to the person who manages SMTO and that Gateway. SMTO should never even try to read a protected field, so this needs to be fixed even after you get past it.

What success looks like

  • You're signed in or past the password step in the app, and SMTO continues the task.

If it still fails

  • If SMTO keeps stopping at the same password step, tell it in the conversation that you have already signed in, and wait for the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste the password or a screenshot of it into the report or the conversation.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A native UI response tried to expose a protected field value.

What this means

  • UI wire validation encountered a secure element whose value_summary was not the required redaction marker and rejected the unsafe value-bearing response. Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.

Why this can happen

  • UI wire validation encountered a secure element whose value_summary was not the required redaction marker and rejected the unsafe value-bearing response.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect only structural redaction diagnostics; never include the rejected secure value in logs, reports or a new read request.

How to fix it

  • This is a redaction defect: a secure element's value_summary was not the fixed secure redaction marker, so wire validation rejected the response. Keep secure values hidden, report a reproducible adapter defect with structural diagnostics only (platform, app, role), and have the user complete the credential step directly in the application.
  • Keep secure values hidden and report a reproducible adapter redaction defect with structural diagnostics only. Credential entry must remain in the application's supported private flow.

Retry and execution caution

  • Secure values cannot be inspected. Ask the user to complete the credential step directly in the application.

How to verify the fix

  • The native response represents secure values only with the fixed redaction marker.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, read secure fields, record input or bypass OS permissions.

Technical notes

  • Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
